items.descriptionEn: Drop into a squat. Hold one ankle with the opposite hand. Fold your other arm to your chest. Staying in the squat and keeping hold of your ankle, twist to turn your chest-hand back/outwards until your elbow is pointing at the sky. Return to the neutral squatting position with your hand on your chest. Repeat movement as required. Repeat on both sides.

items.descriptionEn: The burpee, or squat thrust, is a full body exercise used in strength training and as an aerobic exercise. The basic movement is performed in four steps and known as a four-count burpee: Begin in a standing position. Move into a squat position with your hands on the ground. (count 1) Kick your feet back into a plank position, while keeping your arms extended. (count 2) Immediately return your feet into squat position. (count 3) Stand up from the squat position (count 4)
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：以高位平板支撑姿势开始：背部、手臂和腿均伸直，双手分开与肩同宽。 步骤： 双脚向双臂的方向向前跳，保持背部平直。 双手撑地，双腿跳回高位平板支撑位置。 重复。

items.descriptionEn: Place a barbell in a rack just below shoulder-height. Dip under the bar to put it behind the neck across the top of the back, and grip the bar with the hands wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift the chest up and squeeze the shoulder blades together to keep the straight back throughout the entire movement. Stand up to bring the bar off the rack and step backwards, then place the feet so that they are a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Sit back into hips and keep the back straight and the chest up, squatting down so the hips are below the knees. From the bottom of the squat, press feet into the ground and push hips forward to return to the top of the standing position.
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：站立，双脚分开与肩同宽。 步骤： 将臀部向后移动并弯曲膝盖和臀部降低躯干，直到臀部低于膝盖。 回到初始姿势。 重复。

items.descriptionEn: Grab a wrist roller tool with both hands while standing with your feet about shoulder width apart. If your gym does not have a wrist roller tool, you can easily put one together. All you need is a 5 or 10 pound weight plate, a strong thin rope about 3 feet long and a 6-8 inch stick or bar. Securely fasten the rope to the middle of the bar/stick and tie the other end of the rope to the weight plate. To begin this exercise, grab the bar/stick with both hands using an overhand grip. Extend both arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor. Next, roll the weight up from the floor by rapidly twisting the bar/stick with your hands and wrists. Once the weight reaches the top, slowly lower the plate back to the floor by reversing the motion of your hands and wrists. Repeat (if you can!).
items.author: pwiltrout

items.descriptionEn: Standing side crunches are a dynamic exercise that targets the obliques while improving balance and stability. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands behind your head or holding a dumbbell in one hand. Lean your torso to one side, contracting your obliques, while bringing your elbow toward your hip (or crunching toward the weight if using a dumbbell). Return to the starting position and alternate sides or perform all repetitions on one side before switching.

items.descriptionEn: Benefits of Stationary Bike Cardio Stationary bike cardio is an excellent form of exercise that offers multiple benefits for health and well-being. Here are some of the most notable ones: Improved Cardiovascular Health Strengthens the heart: Regular exercise helps improve the heart's efficiency and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. Increases circulation: It improves blood flow, which can help lower blood pressure. Calorie Burning and Weight Loss Efficient for burning calories: Depending on the intensity, you can burn between 400 and 600 calories per hour. Helps with weight loss: Combined with a balanced diet, stationary bike cardio can be effective for losing weight. Muscle Strengthening Tones the legs: It mainly works the leg muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings and calves. Improves muscular endurance: Over time, you can increase the endurance and strength in your legs. Mental Health Benefits Reduces stress: Exercise releases endorphins, which can improve your mood and reduce stress. Boosts energy: Regular physical activity can raise your energy levels and improve sleep quality.
items.author: Tierrasverdes

items.descriptionEn: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.
items.author: trs1800

items.descriptionEn: The Step Jack is a low-impact plyometric-style move that provides cardiovascular benefits without the joint stress of jumping. It works the entire body, specifically targeting the legs, core, and shoulders. This move is ideal for beginners, individuals with joint sensitivities, or as a dynamic warm-up to gradually elevate the heart rate. Notes (Instructions): ​Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides. ​Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms up above your head. Bring your right foot back to the center and lower your arms. ​Immediately repeat the movement, stepping out with your left foot. ​Continue alternating sides at a steady, rhythmic pace.

items.descriptionEn: Starting position : Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor (or stand/sit upright). Exhalation : Fully exhale all the air from your lungs through your mouth. Contraction : Draw your navel in towards your spine as far as possible, pulling your stomach inward and up under your ribcage. Hold : Hold this isometric contraction without breathing for 10 to 20 seconds. Release : Slowly inhale through your nose to release the tension and relax your abdominals. Repeat : Rest briefly and perform the desired number of sets.
